headline: Turn the AI agent boom into your first real‑world portfolio piece and stand out to recruiters worldwide
why_now: Agentic AI systems are exploding – GitHub activity (96) and growth (94) show massive open‑source momentum, while Hugging Face (92) and news mentions (88) confirm industry buzz. Employers are already hunting talent (job demand 85), so building an agent now gives you immediate career leverage.
study: Complete the "LangChain Fundamentals" course on Coursera (or the free LangChain docs) to learn prompt chaining and tool integration.
Follow the official OpenAI function‑calling guide and build a simple API‑calling bot in Python.
Study two open‑source agent repos on GitHub (e.g., AutoGPT, BabyAGI) – clone, run, and annotate the code.
Read the latest Hugging Face blog posts on tool‑use agents and experiment with a transformer model in a notebook.
Take a short project‑management crash course (e.g., Trello or Notion) to design multi‑step workflows for agents.

build.title: Personal Research Assistant Agent
build.description: An AI agent that takes a natural‑language query (e.g., "Find recent papers on diffusion models and summarize key findings") and automatically searches arXiv via API, extracts abstracts, runs a summarization model, and returns a concise report with citation links. It showcases planning, tool use, and multi‑step reasoning—exactly what employers are looking for.
stack: FastAPI for a simple web UI
deliverables: GitHub repo with clean README, CI badge, and Dockerfile
Live demo hosted on Render or Railway
Technical write‑up (blog post or Medium article) explaining architecture, challenges, and future extensions

publish: Write a concise LinkedIn post with a GIF demo and tag @LangChainAI, @OpenAI, and relevant AI agent hashtags.
Submit the repo to the "Awesome AI Agents" GitHub list and cross‑post on Hacker News (Show HN).
Create a short 2‑minute video walkthrough and share on YouTube and the r/ArtificialIntelligence subreddit.
Add the project to your personal portfolio site and include it in the "Projects" section of your résumé.
skills: Model inference with Hugging Face Transformers
risks: API rate limits or cost spikes if using paid LLM endpoints; mitigate with free tier or local models.
Complexity of multi‑step error handling can lead to brittle agents; invest time in robust exception flows.
Rapidly evolving libraries may cause breakage; lock dependencies and document versioning.
confidence: Based on the strongest signal scores (96–92) and clear industry demand, this recommendation is highly solid for a student aiming to break into AI agent development.
